name: ceremony-use-existing-v1
purpose: Agent Visibility Phase 2, Slice J1-Ceremony (re-scoped by Agent 0 2026-08-14: verify the copy/move identity ceremony by its BEHAVIORAL, user-facing effect + the dialog completion property -- never F1 identity forensics, which reads VaultBrowseDetail/VaultIdentifier catalogue-identification state, NOT VaultIdentity's content-addressed alias registry, and cannot see this ceremony's alias binding at all). Seeds one confirmed Vault root holding a REGISTERED original file (originalStableId) plus an on-disk byte-copy with a size/mtime signature pinned to match it exactly, so VaultIdentity::reconcile() raises a genuine 'likely-copy' ceremony the moment VaultLibrary::republishAtBoot() scans the root -- no scripted trigger, no test-only hook. A seeded Progress resume entry under the original's canonical id proves 'the existing progress remains reachable under the canonical identity' once the ceremony is resolved with Use Existing State.
progressKeyNote: ProgressStore::mapKey(kind,id) = kind + U+001F (ASCII unit separator) + id (native/ProgressStore.h). progressKey above spells that literally as a JSON \u001f escape -- do not paste it as a raw control byte into another JSON file (JSON spec requires control characters escaped; a prior draft of this fixture.json embedded the raw byte by accident and was corrected).
mechanism: VaultLibrary::republishAtBoot() -> VaultScanner::applyPublish() -> VaultIdentity::reconcile(allFacts), called ONCE across every confirmed root's current files (native/engine/VaultScanner.cpp ~line 240). reconcile() computes canonicalsPresent from the CURRENT scan against the identity registry loaded from vault/identity.json at construction. media/OriginalClip/OriginalClip.mp4 (A) has its id ALREADY present in the seeded identity.json (entries[0], with the exact size/mtimeMs the real file on disk carries -- both independently re-verified by an isolated bootstrap capture, see 'provenance' below), so A is NOT 'fresh' this scan -- it stays its own canonical entry. media/OriginalClipCopy/OriginalClipCopy.mp4 (B) has a NEVER-SEEN id (its own path folds into VaultIdentity::computeId's SHA-1 basis), so it IS 'fresh'. reconcile()'s copy-detection loop (native/engine/VaultIdentity.cpp ~line 409) compares each fresh candidate's (size,mtimeMs) against every OTHER entry already in the identity registry (not against other candidates in the same fresh batch -- this only works because A was pre-registered, not scanned fresh alongside B in the same pass): B's size (2771 bytes, byte-identical copy) and mtimeMs (forced via os.utime to 1786660522036, EXACTLY A's registered mtimeMs -- VaultIdentity's likely-copy match requires an EXACT mtimeMs match, no tolerance, unlike its changed-content/rename branch) match A's entry with copyMatches==1 -> a likely-copy ceremony is appended to reconcile()'s result AND remembered in VaultIdentity::m_pending, then persist() emits VaultIdentity::changed(). VaultLibrary connects that signal straight to identityCeremoniesChanged (VaultLibrary.cpp ~line 95), which VaultPage.qml's own ceremony surface (identityCeremonies/identityCeremonyDismissed, VaultPage.qml lines 62-64 and 1317-1333) re-reads and re-opens automatically -- the SAME live-copy pipeline the plan brief names, just proven to surface through the pre-registered-canonical path rather than a live drop into an already-idle, already-scanned watcher (VaultWatcher::processRoot's own per-file idForFile() call has the identical side effect, since it too funnels through VaultIdentity::observeFile(); this fixture uses the boot-scan path because it is deterministic -- no QFileSystemWatcher debounce race against the runner's own wait timeout).
groundTruthCorrection: The program brief's assumption that VaultWatcher::processRoot's idForFile() call would be the trigger is technically accurate (it shares observeFile()'s side effects) but was NOT used here: idForFile() only returns the bare id string, discarding the prompt fields, and if the watcher sees B before any open() call, B's id is registered as a plain fresh entry, permanently short-circuiting observeFile()'s OWN fast path on any later call for the same (path,size,mtime) tuple. The boot-scan/reconcile() path used here has no such race: A is registered in identity.json BEFORE the scan ever runs, so B is unambiguously fresh on its first and only observation.
provenance: originalStableId/newTupleId and identity.json's exact size/mtimeMs were captured empirically, not hand-hashed: an isolated bootstrap session (lanista session run, --seed pointed at an early copy of this exact fixture directory containing ONLY OriginalClip.mp4 plus vault/config.json) was booted, its Vault door opened, and the resulting tagged AppData's vault/identity.json read back directly -- QDir::cleanPath + toLower path normalization inside VaultIdentity::computeId makes hand-computing the SHA-1 basis error-prone (case/separator drift), so the id was taken from the live app's own registration rather than guessed. progress-store.ini's exact byte format (QSettings IniFormat, group 'continue', key 'entries', a doubled-backslash-and-quote-escaped plain string whose content parses back to the same JSON ProgressStore.h's recordProgress() would have written) was likewise round-trip-validated against a live boot before being committed here: a first attempt using the '@ByteArray(...)' type-tag syntax the app itself writes for an EMPTY map was NOT correctly parsed back by QSettings when hand-authored (Progress.get() returned nothing), while a plain escaped-string value (letting QVariant::toByteArray() UTF-8-encode it) round-tripped correctly -- confirmed live via player.pendingSeekSec reading exactly the seeded position after opening the seeded file. tests/fixtures/vault/media/tiny.mp4 (the only real ffmpeg-generated decodable video fixture in this repo, 2771 bytes, 64x64, already used by tst_journey_play_video.cpp/vault_admission_probe_harness/play-video-v1) has a real playback duration too short for PlayerPage.qml's own 'anti-clutter floor' (recordProgress() declines below mpv.position<10s, PlayerPage.qml line 1883) to ever produce a natural resume entry -- seeding progress-store.ini directly is therefore the only way to exercise 'progress follows the canonical identity' without inventing a longer video fixture outside this slice's fence.
reproducibilityCaveat: IMPORTANT, READ BEFORE RE-USING ON A DIFFERENT CHECKOUT OR AFTER A FRESH CLONE/git-clean OF THIS FIXTURE TREE. vault/identity.json and progress-store.ini hard-code a specific mtimeMs (1786660522036) captured from THIS working tree's copy of OriginalClip.mp4. git does not preserve file mtimes on checkout -- a fresh `git clone`, `git checkout --`, or `git clean -fd` of this fixture directory will stamp OriginalClip.mp4 and OriginalClipCopy.mp4 with a NEW mtime at checkout time (not necessarily identical between the two files, and never equal to the hard-coded value), which would silently break the exact-mtime match VaultIdentity::reconcile()'s copy-detection requires -- the ceremony would then simply never fire (both files register as independent fresh entries, itemCount stays 2 but identityCeremonies stays empty, and every ui-wait-for step in journey_ceremony.json would time out honestly rather than pass vacuously). This is the SAME class of fragility every other Vault Lanista fixture in this repo already accepts for its vault/config.json's hard-coded ABSOLUTE machine path (identify-uncertain-v1, vault-browse-five-shapes-v1) -- neither is designed for a portable/CI checkout today, only for repeated runs against Hemanth's own working tree. RECOVERY if this ever goes stale: re-run this fixture.json's own 'provenance' bootstrap procedure (an isolated `lanista session run` against a copy of this directory containing ONLY OriginalClip.mp4 plus vault/config.json, then read the resulting tagged AppData's vault/identity.json back) to recapture the real mtimeMs/id pair, force OriginalClipCopy.mp4's mtime to match via os.utime, and rewrite vault/identity.json + progress-store.ini + this file's originalStableId/newTupleId/shapes fields together in one pass -- never hand-guess the SHA-1.

seededResumePosition.note: 5.5s is intentionally BELOW PlayerPage.qml's resumePromptMinSec (30s, line 139): shouldSkipResumePrompt() short-circuits the Resume/Start-Over overlay for a position this small, so onFileLoaded's own 'silent seek' branch (PlayerPage.qml lines 3088-3090) applies it directly -- player.pendingSeekSec reads exactly 5.5 immediately after the production player mounts for either A or (post-ceremony) B, then mpv.seekExact(5.5) consumes it. A position >=30s was avoided on purpose: tiny.mp4's own real decoded duration is only a few seconds, so any position that large would trip the resumeRestartThreshold (0.80 of mpv.duration) branch instead and silently discard the resume position as 'near finished' -- an artifact of the fixture's short clip, not a ceremony/identity failure. The behavioral proof this scenario asserts on is therefore player.sourceIdentity (stable, decode-independent) plus a direct read of progress-store.ini before/after, with pendingSeekSec captured as corroborating (not gating) evidence.

confirmedRoot: media/ (this fixture directory) -- vault/config.json points a confirmed root directly at the absolute path of this fixture's own media/ subtree, exactly as tests/fixtures/vault/browse-face-smoke-seed and the other journeys' fixtures already do. VaultLibrary::republishAtBoot() scans+publishes this root automatically at boot.

shapes.role: B (byte-identical copy, mtime pinned to A's registered mtimeMs)

negativeControl.purpose: Slice J1-Ceremony's mandatory negative control: prove the resume/alias assertions are a real gate, not vacuous, by taking the OTHER real choice on the SAME ceremony and showing the resume/identity assertions genuinely flip.
negativeControl.direction: Behavioral (not a fixture mutation): choose vaultSeparateCopy instead of vaultUseExistingState on the identical seed. B is then registered as its OWN independent canonical identity (VaultIdentity::decideCeremony only aliases newId->oldId for the same-media/use-existing-state choices; separate-copy/new-media just records the decision and leaves B's id standalone). Opening B afterward reports player.sourceIdentity == B's own newTupleId (never A's originalStableId) and player.pendingSeekSec == -1 (Progress.get('video', B's own id) finds nothing, since progress-store.ini only ever held an entry keyed by A's id) -- both re-derived live, not asserted from memory. Verified live 2026-08-14, session 20260814-042134-2ac94415, preserved at artifacts/visibility-phase2/j1-ceremony/negative-control-separate-copy/.
negativeControl.howRun: Re-run the isolated session against the SAME --seed fixture directory (a fresh tag), replacing the 'choose vaultUseExistingState' step with 'choose vaultSeparateCopy', then repeat only the open-B/read-player leg with a bounded wait -- sourceIdentity must NOT equal originalStableId and pendingSeekSec must NOT equal the seeded position. Restore by re-running the ordinary use-existing-state scenario and confirming green again.

note: OriginalClip.mp4 and OriginalClipCopy.mp4 are the SAME 2771-byte real ffmpeg-generated decodable MP4 (tests/fixtures/vault/media/tiny.mp4, 64x64, already used by tst_journey_play_video.cpp and vault_admission_probe_harness) -- copied byte-for-byte, with the copy's mtime forced (os.utime) to exactly the original's registered mtimeMs so VaultIdentity's likely-copy match (exact size+mtime, no tolerance) fires deterministically every run.
